title: The Wedding Night
hook: On the night Rumi died, his friends called it a wedding.

segments.fa: چون جان تو می‌ستانی چون شکر است مردن
segments.en: When it is You who takes my soul, dying is sweet as sugar.

segments.fa: با تو ز جان شیرین شیرین‌تر است مردن
segments.en: With You, dying is sweeter than sweet life itself.

tafsir: Rumi died in Konya on the seventeenth of December, 1273.
In this ghazal, death is not a thief. The Beloved is the one who comes.
So dying becomes sugar, sweeter even than life.
His followers call that night Shab-e Arus, the wedding night.
It is the night the soul meets the one it longed for.
Every December, in Konya, they still keep it with music and turning.

outro.say: That was our serial, Shams and Rumi. Next, Rumi from the original Persian, one verse a week. Follow The Guest House.
